prompt: A phone app finds a contact's number by their name without scanning the whole list.
why: You give a name and get a number back without scanning. Looking up a value by a key in one step is a hash map.
trap: A set only says yes or no; here a value comes back.

prompt: A word counter keeps, for each word, how many times it has appeared.
tells: for each word, how many times
why: Each word is a key and its count is the value, updated as you go. Keeping a value for each key is a hash map.
trap: A set would lose the counts.

prompt: A shop looks up a price by product code in one step.
why: The code is the key and the price is the value, found in one step. Key-to-value lookup is a hash map.
trap: Codes aren't positions in a list.

prompt: A cache remembers each URL's page so the second request for it is instant.
why: The URL is the key and the saved page is the value, so a repeat request is answered instantly. A cache is a hash map from requests to results.
trap: It returns the page, not just 'seen it'.

prompt: As you walk through the numbers, you remember each number's position so you can find its partner later.
why: You store each number with its position so a later lookup finds the partner in one step. Remembering a value for each key is a hash map.
trap: A set would lose the position.

prompt: A dictionary app maps each word to its definition.
tells: maps each word to its definition
why: Each word maps to one definition, and you look it up by the word. Word in, definition out is a hash map.
trap: Alphabetical order isn't needed for one lookup.
